procedural_markers.text: All right. That may be admitted. Counsel, can I see you sidebar just for a second? ([06:09:46](https://www.rev.com/app/transcript/NmE3MWNiZTFhNjZmN2RkZjg4YTQ3NzkxM3I4RlVZNTZCWVVT/o/VEMwMTg3Mjg4MjU3?ts=22186.08)) All right, Commonwealth.

procedural_markers.speaker: Speaker 24
procedural_markers.text: Thank  you. Trooper Melo, just in relation to now what's been marked as  Exhibit 151, the Brown Journal, and just noting that when the journal  opens to the first page, there's no dates on it, correct?

procedural_markers.speaker: Speaker 24
procedural_markers.text: And  there's one on November 18th. And November 18th, that page reads, "It's  like I'm so desperate to get a mental break from taking care of  everyone that my mind is trying to make something physically wrong with  me." You recall reviewing that in the journal?

procedural_markers.speaker: Speaker 24
procedural_markers.text: This journal I'm holding up, Exhibit number 147, is that familiar to you?

procedural_markers.speaker: Speaker 24
procedural_markers.text: Okay.  And this third journal that you reviewed after the search warrant,  Exhibit number 50, the yellow journal with Callan Clancy's name on it,  do you recall that?

procedural_markers.speaker: Mr. Reddington
procedural_markers.text: And  then the statement started getting smaller and smaller as time went by.  One occasion, "It's like I'm desperate to get a mental break from  taking care of everyone. My mind is trying to make something physically  wrong with me. My mind never shuts off. It's constantly thinking of the  next thing someone needs. I can't shut it off. I desperately want to go  back to work, but now I don't know how I'm going to function and it  worries me." Wrote that, right?

procedural_markers.speaker: Speaker 23
procedural_markers.text: Okay. Redirect?

procedural_markers.speaker: Speaker 23
procedural_markers.text: All right. Thank you, sir. You may step down. Counsel, can I see you at sidebar? ([06:24:54](https://www.rev.com/app/transcript/NmE3MWNiZTFhNjZmN2RkZjg4YTQ3NzkxM3I4RlVZNTZCWVVT/o/VEMwMTg3Mjg4MjU3?ts=23094.21)) All  right. So members of the jury, we're going to break at this point till  tomorrow. All right? Talking to counsel, my expectation is we'd have a  similar schedule tomorrow. The hope would be it will go in the morning  and it should go into the afternoon, but just to give you the, that's  the best estimate that we have. All right? And so, I'm going to excuse  you till tomorrow. Remember I'm going to ask you those questions. Don't  listen to anything. Don't talk about this. Don't take any road trips or  do any research on this. Put this out of your head as best you can till  tomorrow morning. Hopefully the rain has stopped and we'll see everybody  tomorrow. Thank you so much for all your work here today. Thank you.

procedural_markers.speaker: Speaker 23
procedural_markers.text: All right. So we'll be in recess on this until tomorrow morning at 9:00. Thank you.
